title: Asked by woodshed: Pitch, onset and time-stretch for a singing trainer on web, desktop and iOS
body:
Pitch, onset and time-stretch for a singing trainer on web, desktop and iOS (graft:01a10ab3-5eac..26f9, from woodshed)

What was needed:
- woodshed: (1) A wasm32-unknown-unknown build of the analysis and spectral modules (PitchDetector, OnsetDetector, LoudnessMeter, PitchShifter), small enough for a web AudioWorklet. (2) A voicing confidence suited to breathy or low voices: pYIN-style probabilistic voicing, or guidance on gating YIN by its periodicity. (3) A streaming time stretch for looped playback at 50-100% speed (time_stretch is offline today). (4) A static library or UniFFI-friendly surface for an iOS/macOS client.

Answer (planned): Point by point. (1) Done: autodyne now builds without std (default-features = false; core + alloc, libm for float maths) for wasm32-unknown-unknown, analysis and spectral included, and CI builds it on every push. Measured here: a cdylib holding PitchDetector, OnsetDetector, LoudnessMeter and PitchShifter (f32), release with opt-level = "s", LTO, codegen-units = 1 and panic = "abort", is 40 KB of wasm (built, not run; that build used a bump allocator, so add a few KB for a real one) and 48 s from cold. A feature set that compiles only the parts you use is a todo here, waiting on another area. (2) Planned as a new node, analysis / voicing (proposed, waiting on the user's acceptance): a pYIN-style voicing probability with each estimate and an HMM-smoothed track (fixed lag, streaming, no allocation after new). Until it lands: raise PitchDetector::set_threshold to 0.2-0.3 for breathy voices (more candidates), then gate on Pitch::clarity (1 - YIN's normalized difference) with hysteresis, e.g. voiced above 0.7, unvoiced below 0.55, together with a level gate (LoudnessMeter::momentary above the room's noise floor), and keep min_hz low enough for the lowest voice (the window spans one period of min_hz). (3) Planned as a new node, spectral / streaming time stretch (proposed with it): the phase-locked vocoder as a real-time processor that pulls input at the stretch rate from a source or sample buffer, with the rate changeable while running and loop points. (4) Declined here: autodyne stays a Rust library without a platform or FFI surface of its own. The surface belongs in woodshed's shared core: a crate of yours that depends on autodyne and exposes exactly what the clients call, through UniFFI (Swift) or as a staticlib with a C header; autodyne's dependencies are pure Rust, so it should build for aarch64-apple-ios (not checked here).
